newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs three veterans bills.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs three veterans bills.

text.p: President Clinton Wednesday signed three bills that he said would ensure veterans' benefits keep pace with inflation and improve other veteran programmes and benefits.
As part of a series of bill signings closing out the current session of Congress, Clinton signed the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 1996.

It authorises a cost-of-living increase on Dec. 1 for recipients of veterans' disability compensation and other programmes. It will be identical to the raise Social Security recipients will receive on Jan. 1 and will go to about 2.3 million veterans with disabilities.
Clinton also signed the Veterans' Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 1996, which Clinton said in a statement will improve the veterans health care system.
For example, it authorises the Veterans Affairs Department to furnish comprehensive medical services to all veterans.

A third veterans bill Clinton signed is called the Veterans' Benefits Improvements Act of 1996 which expands and extends numerous veterans education, housing, life insurance and employment and training benefits.

In a separate area, Clinton also signed the Railroad Unemployment Insurance Amendments Act of 1996 which he said will bring unemployment benefits for railroad workers in line with benefits for other workers.
